d: Sixteen years after Obamacare was introduced, healthcare affordability is emerging as a key issue ahead of the US midterm elections. Medicaid cuts, rising insurance premiums and uncertainty over federal subsidies are putting millions of Americans under pressure. For some, the cost of coverage is so high that they are delaying or avoiding medical treatment altogether. Firstpost’s James Gooderson brings you a ground report from Washington DC, speaking to healthcare professionals and exploring whether rising healthcare costs could influence voters at the ballot box.
